Hannah / Laura — reviewed the Clearsky redlines and your draft change order. High-level legal flags and suggested edits below. I put inline suggestions in the document and summarized the non-negotiables here so we can triage with the customer.

1) Proration / Billing
- Redline: change "prorated" to a defined "Proration Calculation" clause that uses calendar days in the invoice month; specify rounding rule.
- Suggest limiting retrospective true-up adjustments to a single subsequent quarter unless there is clear evidence of measurement error. This reduces perpetual reconciliation scope.

2) SLA & service credits
- Acceptable to provide a 30-day remediation period. For credits, propose a cap (e.g., 5% monthly fee credited) for the first 6 months after capacity increase to limit financial exposure.
- Insert language tying credits to measurable latency percentiles (p95) for the impacted endpoints — ops will need to provide target numbers.

3) Data retention & cache warming behavior
- Clearsky's redlines request persistent KV cache warming during phase-in. Legal requests we add a sentence clarifying that cache contents are ephemeral and customer data retention follows the MSA data retention exhibit; any pre-warmed state is at Clearsky's configuration.

4) Implementation assistance fee & scope
- Add a small SOW Exhibit listing acceptance criteria for the cutover and rollback plan (who signs acceptance, metrics to verify). Keep implementation fee refundable only if we materially miss timelines due to Redwood fault.

5) DocuSign / signature flow
- We prefer to execute the change order with a single signature from authorized reps and reference the original MSA by contract id. If Clearsky requires countersignature ordering, confirm whether their procurement system requires vendor-first signing.

6) Timeline risk
- Customer target Jul 10 is tight. Operationally we can do it if legal comments are accepted quickly. Recommend the Ops sync and a follow-up 1-hour redline call with Clearsky legal tomorrow.

I attached a marked PDF with inline edits (sent to Hannah directly).

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
